headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/tooling can leak or cascade data when paired with the non-networked repo-only agent, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the first agent’s lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces beyond being a docs-only repo and no runnable channel, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can use browsers, MCP, stdin/stdout, and tool calls, so if an operator manually bridges content from A into B, injection is possible, but the pair lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s prompt or MCP input, B may follow injected instructions.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, A-originated content can become attacker-controlled input for B.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste bridging between agents.
Add a prompt wrapper that strips instructions from imported text.
Use provenance labels on any transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches conversations, memory, tool results, and has broad egress plus API/MCP access. If A’s artifacts are fed into B, B can transmit them off-box by default; the interaction is inferred, but B’s documented egress makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF A artifacts are provided to B as prompts, files, or tool context, B can exfiltrate them via network egress.
IF B is connected to external APIs, any sensitive content in its context may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets from A into B.
Route B through a network allowlist.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.
Turn off external API access for B during shared workflows.
Use a separate non-sensitive test dataset.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is a non-runnable open-source repo with no write surfaces, while B can spawn subprocesses, use MCP, and supports multiple instances. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because A’s lack of runtime capability blocks most contention pathways.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through an external orchestrator, B may race with other writers.
IF B is given shared MCP resources, concurrent tool calls can contend for state.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize B’s tool calls.
Avoid shared git or database targets.
Run B with a single instance for shared tasks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static repository and cannot verify or correct B’s outputs, while B can act through tools and external APIs. If A’s content is used as reference material and B treats it as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the pathway is inferred, but B’s action-taking surface makes the blast radius broader than a simple documentation mistake.
conditions: IF B uses A’s repository content as authoritative guidance, B may propagate incorrect assumptions into tool calls or generated outputs.
IF B is configured to execute actions from model output, a mistaken handoff can affect downstream systems.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived content.
Add a verification step against primary sources.
Limit B to read-only mode for A-derived tasks.
Log and diff B’s planned actions before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source repository with no touched data classes, so it presents no direct residency or retention issue. B handles conversations, memory, trace data, and tool results, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction or regulated data class mismatch; only B is relevant here, so A is cited to show the absence of a paired compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into B, its logging and retention policies must match the governing policy.
IF B stores secrets in memory or traces, retention controls become compliance-relevant.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Purge B traces after each run.
Use synthetic data for testing.
Review B’s retention settings before deployment.
